items.title: Detention v. arrest: Beyond labels
items.summary: The distinction between detention and arrest is often treated as a matter of terminology. In practice, however, it concerns something far more fundamental: the extent to which the State can deprive an individual of personal liberty while avoiding the procedural safeguards that the law attaches to an arrest. The terms custody, detention and arrest are often used interchangeably in ordinary speech, but the law places each at a different point on the same spectrum of restraint. 'Custody' is the widest of the three. As the Supreme Court held in Niranjan Singh v. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote , a person is in custody the moment they submit to the control of the police or the court, whether or not any formal arrest has been recorded. ‘Arrest’ is the narrowest and most consequential of the three, since it requires an accusation or suspicion of an offence and, once made, immediately triggers the full suite of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) safeguards. ‘Detention’ sits between the two: it is custody exercised without an accusation, whether for brief inquiry under BNSS Section 170 , through the security proceedings in BNSS Sections 125 to 129 , or, in its most severe executive form, under preventive detention statutes such as the National Security Act (NSA). The Supreme Court drew the custody and arrest line most sharply in Directorate of Enforcement v. Deepak Mahajan , holding that every arrest involves custody but not every custody amounts to arrest. Further, the arrest and detention line has been drawn in State of Punjab v. Ajaib Singh , where the Court held that restraint of a person not accused of any offence falls outside the meaning of arrest under Article 22 . The thin difference matters in practice precisely because each point on the spectrum carries a different and sharply diminishing set of procedural protections for the person restrained. What is an arrest? Arrest, per se, is not defined in any exhaustive manner under the statute. However, it is understood as a serious restraint upon an individual’s personal liberty based on an accusation or suspicion of an offence. It brings an individual within the coercive framework of criminal law and activates a series of constitutional and statutory safeguards. items.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association calls off work suspension, district bar bodies also to resume work
items.summary: Various Bar bodies in Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh including the Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association have decided to suspend their strike against the implementation of Legal Defence Counsel System (LADCS) in the trial courts. The announcement comes a day after a meeting was held between a joint action committee of district associations and acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra . Other judges were also present at the meeting. Sources said bar leaders were told that the issues being raised by them can only be addressed by the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). They were also assured that every aspect relating to the implementation of the scheme would be examined and addressed. In order to end the stalemate, members of the joint action committee, the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana and the representatives of the High Court Bar Association are likely to meet Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant next week. In a notice issued this evening, the High Court Bar Association said majority of the district Bar associations have resolved to resume judicial work on August 3. Accordingly, it requested its members too to resume their professional work from Monday. It expressed a hope that concerns of lawyers shall receive a positive and meaningful resolution in the meeting with CJI. Meanwhile, joint action committee said the strike of the district bar bodies would remain suspended only on August 03, with next course of action depending on the outcome of the meeting with CJI. Lawyers, particularly in Punjab, have been on strike for nearly a month against LADCS, alleging that the scheme has created a parallel State-funded criminal defence system which was affecting the practice of independent advocates. Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association also joined the striking lawyers this week and suspended work at the High Court. Lawyers also staged protests at the high court to express solidarity with the trial court lawyers. The strike, which was initially limited to Punjab, also spread to many district of Haryana and Chandigarh this week. The High Court recently issued a circular to address some of the grievances highlighted by the lawyers but made it clear that there would no rollback of the scheme since it is being implemented across the country by NALSA. items.title: Stray cattle on roads an invitation to death: Supreme Court calls for compensation policy for accident victims
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday asked the Central and State governments to put in place a mechanism for compensating victims of stray cattle accidents and for ensuring better implementation of laws governing stray cattle [ Nisha v Municipal Council Sangrur & Ors ]. A Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and NK Singh passed the direction while flagging the danger posed by stray cattle to both human and animal life on highways and roads. “Stray cattle on highways are a constant invitation to death. After all, they are not meant to be natural speed breakers, placed willy-nilly on the National Highways, roads and streets,” it observed. The Bench added that such incidents often prove fatal for motorists and pedestrians alike, and can occur even without a vehicle involved. “It is not only these animals but also the humans that at times meet the most painful of ends while driving merrily along for no other reason but the fact that all of a sudden, an animal comes in front of the vehicle leading to a collision,” it noted. Citing government data, the Court noted that animal attacks killed 1,130 people across India in 2018, 1,425 in 2019, and 1,305 in 2020. It proceeded to ask the Centre and States to frame a mechanism to compensate victims of stray cattle accidents, mandate cattle tagging and ensure better implementation of laws governing stray animals. He sustained a serious head injury. Vijay sought compensation from the authorities during his lifetime, but the Deputy Commissioner of Sangrur declined his request solely on the ground that the department did not have funds available for such compensation - without ever disputing that the incident had occurred. Vijay passed away some years later. After his death, Nisha approached the Punjab and Haryana High Court. items.title: Bihar policy to restrict compassionate appointment to divorced or deserted daughters cannot be sustained: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently held that the Bihar government's 2014 policy classifying only divorced or deserted daughters as eligible for compassionate appointment cannot be sustained in law [Sayara Khatoon @ Shayara Khatoon & Anr v State of Bihar & Ors.]. The Court said there can be no presumption in law that a daughter severs ties with her parental family merely because she is married. In an order passed on July 23, Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale set aside a Patna High Court judgment as well as the Bihar government's order rejecting a widow's request for compassionate appointment for her daughter following her husband's death. The Court held that restricting compassionate appointment to only divorced or deserted daughters could not be sustained in law. " On a perusal of the policy, we find that classification restricting eligibility only to a divorced or deserted daughter cannot be sustained in the eye of law. There cannot be a presumption in law that, after marriage, a daughter severs her ties with her parental family and resides with husband in her matrimonial home. " It further reiterated that any classification differentiating a daughter from a son is unconstitutional. Justice M.M. Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B. Varale The case arose after a widow sought compassionate appointment for her daughter following her husband's death. The claim was rejected under the Bihar government's policy dated December 10, 2014. The policy made only divorced or deserted daughters eligible for compassionate appointment. The authorities also relied on an objection raised by the widow's brother. The widow and her daughter challenged the rejection before the Patna High Court, which dismissed their plea. Aggrieved by the decision, they approached the Supreme Court. Before the Supreme Court, they submitted that the widow's brother had later furnished a no-objection certificate. They argued that the first ground for rejection no longer survived. They also challenged the 2014 policy as violative of Article 14. The State contended that compassionate appointment is governed by policy and that a married daughter is ordinarily expected to leave her parental home after marriage. items.title: Bail can't be denied just to "teach a lesson" or satisfy society's conscience: Jammu and Kashmir High Court
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on Friday observed that courts cannot deny bail to a person accused of a crime only to “teach him a lesson” or to satisfy the conscience of society [ Nisar Ahmed Joo v. UT of J&K ]. Justice Sanjay Dhar explained that such an approach would amount to pre-trial punishment, which is impermissible in law. The Court made the observation while granting bail to a man accused of raping a girl aged around 16-17 years old in 2024. The Court granted him bail after noting that the allegations against him appeared to be highly doubtful. "Merely because the petitioner is facing trial for heinous offences which entail punishment extending upto life imprisonment, is not a good enough reason to deny concession of bail to him when his, prima facie, involvement in the alleged crime is highly doubtful. The concession of bail to the petitioner, in these circumstances, cannot be denied just to teach him a lesson or to satisfy the conscience of the society as it would amount to inflicting pre-trial punishment upon them, which is impermissible in law," the Court said. Justice Sanjay Dhar The Court also noted that since the all the material witnesses cited by the prosecution had already been examined by a trial court, there was little chance of the accused influencing any witness or tampering with evidence. The bail plea was filed by one Nissar Ahmad Joo, who is facing trial in a case registered under Sections 137(2) (kidnapping) and 64 (rape) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 3 (penetrative sexual assault) and 4 (punishment) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). The case is tied to a complaint filed by a teenage girl's father, who reported her missing on November 11, 2024. The girl was found on November 17, 2024. In an initial statement given to a judicial magistrate, she alleged that she had been sexually assaulted by four different persons at different locations over several days after leaving home with friends. Based on the girl's statement, police arrested three accused, namely Mohammad Ashraf Sheikh, Chaman Lal and Basharat Ahmad Shora, on November 29, 2024. Later, the police arrested a fourth person, Nisar Ahmad, in May 2025. However, at the stage of trial, the victim/ prosecutrix is said to have disowned her earlier allegations and said that she did not want to pursue the case against the accused men. items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently restrained a Gujarati newspaper from using the name ‘Saurashtra Aaj Tak’ after finding that it amounted to passing off and was likely to create an impression that it was associated with the Aaj Tak news channel [ TV Today Network v. Saurashtra Aaj Tak and Another ]. Justice Mini Pushkarna directed the newspaper to adopt another name that is neither similar nor deceptively similar to the ‘Aaj Tak’ mark owned by TV Today Network. The Court observed that the words ‘Aaj Tak’ had acquired a secondary meaning and had become distinctive of the news dissemination services offered by TV Today Network. “ The manner of the use of the words ‘Saurashtra Aaj Tak’, with more emphasis on the words ‘Aaj Tak’, leaves no doubt that the respondent/defendant (the newspaper) is trying to pass off its newspaper on the goodwill and reputation of the appellant/plaintiff (TV Today), ” the Court added. Justice Mini Pushkarna The July 30 judgment came in an appeal filed by TV Today against a February 2012 decision of a Delhi trial court. The dispute arose after TV Today learnt in December 2002 that a Gujarati newspaper titled ‘Saurashtra Aaj Tak’ had been launched from Rajkot and was being circulated in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat. TV Today issued a legal notice in January 2003 before filing a passing-off suit in April that year. The trial court had permitted the newspaper to continue using ‘Saurashtra Aaj Tak’, subject to prominently publishing a disclaimer stating that it had no connection or association with Aaj Tak of TV Today Network. It had also restrained the newspaper from expressly or impliedly claiming such an association. TV Today then moved the High Court, challenging the trial court's refusal to grant a complete injunction against the Gujarati newspaper. The High Court noted that Aaj Tak was first launched as a news programme on Doordarshan in 1995 and became a 24-hour Hindi news channel in 2000. The mark 'Aaj Tak' was subsequently registered in Classes 38 and 41 in the name of TV Today’s holding company, Living Media India Limited. It was also declared a well-known trademark during the pendency of the appeal. The Court found that although ‘Aaj’ (today) and ‘Tak’ (news) may individually be descriptive or dictionary words, their combination was entitled to protection because of its long and continuous use in connection with the news channel. items.title: Delhi riots: Sessions court sentences Tahir Hussain to life in jail for murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma
items.summary: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain and four other convicts to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the Delhi Riots of 2020. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Parveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court rejected the prosecution's plea for death penalty and instead sentenced the five convicts to life in jail. The Court said that while the barbarity of the crime was "nauseating and sickening", the convicts -- Tahir Hussain, Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas -- are not beyond reformation. It observed that the crime was committed when Delhi was going through communal riots, and it shows utmost brutality. It said that Sharma was sucked in by a murderous mob baying for blood. “The savagery did not end there [with the murder of Sharma]. Instead, the body was strapped like an animal as if the hatred has still not satiated. The body was then thrown into the nallah (drain). The barbarity with which this horrendous crime was committed, is nauseating and sickening. Therefore this is an aggravating circumstance of immense magnitude… The crime test, thus, tilts the case towards rarest of rare cases,” the court said. However, the Court added that the police failed to establish that the convicts have a violent disposition. “It has also not been shown that any of the convicts previously were involved in any violent crime. The conduct of convicts, Tahir Hussain,Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas, while in custody, except for minor infractions, has been entirely satisfactory. This indicates that they can be disciplined and made to follow rules,” Judge Singh reasoned. Therefore, all the convicts were sentenced to life imprisonment. The Delhi Police had sought the death penalty for Hussain and other convicts, stating that Sharma’s murder was “cold-blooded” and brutal. “Those who want mercy should also show mercy. They have no evidence to show that any mercy was shown by any person to carry this person to a hospital,” the Delhi Police counsel told the Court. The plea for death penalty was opposed by the counsel representing Hussain and other convicts - Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas. It was stated that the death penalty can be awarded only in the rarest of rare cases. items.title: Rajasthan police tells High Court it will close cheating case against Sanjay Leela Bhansali, others
items.summary: Rajasthan Police has decided to file a closure report in a cheating case registered last year against filmmaker Sanjay Leela Bhansali and two members of his production team in connection with the film Love & War starring Ranbir Kapoor, Vicky Kaushal and Alia Bhatt. The information was submitted made before Justice Baljinder Singh Sandhu in Rajasthan High Court on July 17 during the hearing of a petition moved by the three accused for quashing of the First Information Report (FIR). State counsel said the police after thorough investigation in the matter has proposed to file a negative final report before the competent court. The filing of a negative final report indicates that the investigating agency has not found sufficient material to prosecute the accused. The trial court will now consider whether to accept the police report or not. In view of the submission, the High Court declined to entertain proceed further with the petition filed by Bhansali, production manager Utkarsh Bali and Arvinder Gill for quashing the case. “ This Court has considered the matter and in view thereof, is not inclined to interfere in the matter," the Bench said while dismissing the plea by the accused. However, it granted the petitioners a liberty to raise all their contentions before the competent court at the appropriate stage. The case arose from an FIR registered at the Bichhwal Police Station in Bikaner on September 1, 2025. It invoked Sections 318(4), 61(2), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating, criminal conspiracy, intentional insult and criminal intimidation. The complaint was lodged by Prateek Raj Mathur, founder of a film production and hospitality company that provides line-production services. Mathur alleged that Bali contacted him in November 2024 and represented that he would be engaged as line producer for Love & War. According to the complaint, he was asked to make security and logistical arrangements for the production team’s proposed visit to Rajasthan. Mathur claimed that after he began making arrangements and incurred expenses, he was informed that the production house could not confirm any collaboration with him. items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday stayed two orders issued by the Chairman of the Bar Council of India (BCI) constituting an interim authority to carry out certain functions of the Bar Council of Kerala (BCK) until the recently elected XIIIth State Council conducts its first meeting [ Yeshwanth Shenoy v Bar Council of India ]. One of the newly elected BCK members, advocate Yeshwanth Shenoy, has questioned how such an interim arrangement can continue after the newly elected council (XIII Bar Council of Kerala) was notified in the Kerala Gazette on June 16, 2026. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas today agreed to hear two connected writ petitions, including the one by Shenoy, challenging the interim arrangement put in place by the BCI chairman. items.title: Shraddha Walkar murder: Delhi HC rejects plea by brother to fix deadline for trial
items.summary: The Delhi High Court today declined to entertain a plea seeking the time-bound conclusion of the trial against Aftab Poonawalla, who is accused of murdering and dismembering his live-in partner Shraddha Walkar in 2022. A Bench of Justice Madhu Jain held that no such directions are required since the trial court was already conducting day-to-day proceedings and making every endeavour to conclude the case as soon as possible. Justice Madhu Jain The Court was dealing with a plea filed by Walkar's brother. He told the Court that Walkar's family have not been able to perform her final rites because her body's remains were still in the custody of the investigating agency and the trial court. These remains will only be handed over once the trial is over. Walkar's brother, however, flagged concerns that the trial is unlikely to finish in the next five years if it continues at the current pace. The trial court's own order showed 48 witnesses were still to be examined, his counsel said. The State's counsel informed that of 222 total witnesses, 157 had already been examined. Six examinations remained pending, including four overseas data witnesses from Google and Bumble, and one nodal officer. Fourteen witnesses remain to be cross-examined, he added. "The matter is going to be on day to day basis," said Senior counsel Amit Prasad, representing the Delhi Police. He further told the Court that the trial court, in a May 2026 order, had already put the accused on notice to ensure his counsel appeared regularly, and that hearings were being held daily except on weekends. Recording these submissions, the Court held that it was evident the trial court was making every effort to conclude the trial expeditiously, and that no further directions were warranted since day-to-day proceedings were already underway. The petitioner's counsel pressed the Court to pass some direction for a time-bound conclusion, but the request was not entertained. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed the arrest of former Tamil Nadu Minister and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MLA V Senthil Balaji in a corruption case concerning alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC). A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi passed the interim order while hearing Balaji's appeal against the Madras High Court's refusal to grant him anticipatory bail in the case. The top court also directed Balaji to cooperate with the ongoing investigation, deposit his passport, and ensure that no witnesses are influenced till further orders. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) registered against Balaji and six others concerns alleged irregularities in liquor procurement, transport contracts, bar licences and other administrative decisions within TASMAC between 2021 and 2025. Balaji had served as Tamil Nadu’s Minister for Prohibition and Excise during part of this period. Following the registration of the First Information Report (FIR), DVAC officials conducted searches at more than 40 locations across Tamil Nadu, including Balaji’s residence in Karur and premises linked to his former aides and other accused persons. Apart from Balaji, the case names former TASMAC Managing Director S Visakan, former senior regional managers T Ramadurai Murugan and R Panneerselvam, Balaji’s former personal assistant Bhaskar, alleged middleman Rathesh Raj Shanmugavel and S Karthik. According to the DVAC, bar licence tenders were allegedly manipulated through cartelisation, proxy ownership and the use of consecutively numbered demand drafts. The agency has alleged that Rathesh Raj exercised undue influence over TASMAC’s operations, including approval of liquor brands, transfers of officials and allotment of bar licences. Visakan allegedly acted on Rathesh Raj’s directions, which were said to have originated from Balaji. The agency has further alleged that certain distilleries generated unaccounted cash by inflating invoices relating to used liquor bottles. items.title: Supreme Court stays CIC order declaring NSE a public authority under RTI Act
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed a 2007 order of the Central Information Commission (CIC) declaring the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) a public authority under the Right to Information Act (RTI Act). [ National Stock Exchange vs. CIC]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the interim order while issuing notice on NSE’s appeal against a Delhi High Court judgment that upheld the applicability of the RTI Act to the stock exchange. “ In the meantime, the execution and operation of the order passed by the Central Information Commissioner dated 7th June, 2007 shall remain stayed, ” the Supreme Court ordered. The CIC had declared stock exchanges, including the NSE, to be public authorities under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act. It had also directed the NSE and the Jaipur Stock Exchange to establish a mechanism for handling applications under the transparency law. The High Court had upheld the same, leading to the appeal before the Supreme Court. During the hearing, the apex court observed that transparency has assumed increasing importance. “ These are days of transparency ,” the Bench remarked. The Court also orally indicated that the protection enjoyed by the NSE against the CIC order may not continue indefinitely. “ This shield is not going to stand for very long anyhow ,” it said. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The dispute dates back to 2007, when a full Bench of the CIC ruled that stock exchanges fell within the RTI Act. The NSE challenged that order before the Delhi High Court and secured an interim stay on July 4, 2007. On April 15, 2010, Justice Sanjiv Khanna dismissed the NSE’s petition and upheld the CIC’s conclusion. Justice Khanna held that although the NSE was incorporated as a private company, its recognition under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 transformed it into an authority performing public functions. The NSE then filed an appeal before a Division Bench, which stayed the single-judge’s judgment on May 4, 2010. That appeal remained pending for nearly 16 years. On July 1 this year , a Division Bench of Justices C Hari Shankar and Om Prakash Shukla dismissed the appeal and affirmed Justice Khanna’s ruling. items.title: Supreme Court to grant Omar Abdullah divorce after marriage dispute settled
items.summary: The Supreme Court was informed on Friday that Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah has resolved his divorce dispute with his estranged wife, Payal Abdullah, through mediation. A Bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe disposed of the appeal after Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal , appearing for Omar Abdullah, informed the Court that all disputes between the parties had been amicably resolved. "Both of them have embraced freedom. It's all settled. Lordships may grant divorce. All other matters will be withdrawn," submitted Sibal. Responding to the submission, the Bench observed, "That's good. We will dispose it of on those terms." Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe Omar and Payal got married in September 1994, but have been living separately for a long time. Omar's divorce plea was first rejected by a family court on August 30, 2016. The family court had held that he failed to prove that his marriage had irretrievably broken down. It also said the politician could not prove his claims of "cruelty" or "desertion" and that he was not able to explain a single circumstance that made it impossible for him to continue the relationship with Payal. Omar had then moved the Delhi High Court. However, the High Court also rejected the divorce plea, which prompted the politician to approach the Supreme Court for relief. He had sought the Court's intervention under Article 142 of the Constitution, which empowers the top court to pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in a matter. This provision has been invoked by the Supreme Court in the past to dissolve marriages that were beyond repair (irretrievably broken down marriages). In August 2024, the Supreme Court had referred the matter to mediation after both sides agreed to explore an amicable settlement. items.title: Rajasthan High Court imposes ₹5 lakh costs on Centre for wrongly suspending IRS officer over 'rude behaviour'
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court at Jodhpur recently ordered the Central government and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs to pay ₹5,00,000 in exemplary costs to an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer who was arbitrarily suspended from service. [Manmeet Singh Ahluwalia v. Union of India] A Bench of Justices Munnuri Laxman and Anuroop Singhi quashed a Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) that upheld the suspension order against Manmeet Singh Ahluwalia, a Deputy Commissioner of Customs and GST. The Court held that the allegations against the officer arising from a residential dispute involving his family members and certain COVID-era leave lapses amounted to a "gross exaggeration of trivial deviations" that could never justify the extreme step of prolonged suspension. It said, "The extensions of suspension caused great mental agony and resulted destruction of his bright service carrier. The petitioner suffered deprivation of his promotional avenues. An incident between the families resulted in ruining the career of a highranking officer. This is a clear case of vendetta by higher officials." The dispute traces back to a 2019 altercation at the officer's government accommodation in Delhi involving his mother and widowed sister, which led to complaints, an eviction notice and his transfer to Jodhpur. Further complaints followed from officers residing in the same residential colony, along with allegations of unauthorised absence during the pandemic. The officer was suspended in May 2021 and the suspension was extended twice, before being allowed to lapse and formally revoked in August 2022, after which a chargesheet was issued against him. The officer had approached the CAT challenging the extension orders, seeking his promotion and consequential benefits, but the Tribunal dismissed his plea, prompting the writ petition before the High Court. The Court found that the principal allegations were either unconnected to the officer's official duties or attributable to family members rather than the officer himself. It held that neither charge, even if proved, would warrant dismissal or removal from service. It noted that suspension is a drastic measure meant only for grave misconduct and that the disciplinary authority already possessed all relevant material at the time of the initial suspension itself, making the extensions unnecessary. items.title: Karnataka HC suspends life sentence of ex-Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni in Yogesh Gowda murder case, grants bail
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Friday suspended the life sentence imposed on former Congress MLA Vinay Kulkarni and eight other convicts in the 2016 murder of BJP leader Yogesh Gowda, holding that they are entitled to be released on bail pending disposal of their criminal appeals. A Bench of Justices Mohammad Nawaz and G Basavaraja also suspended the seven-year sentence imposed on suspended police officer Channakeshava B Tingarikar (Accused No. 19) and ordered his release on bail. Justice Mohammed Nawaz and Justice G Basavaraja During the hearing, Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) counsel Rahul Reddy pointed out that when Kulkarni had earlier been enlarged on bail, one of the conditions imposed was that he should not enter Dharwad district. The Bench, however, observed, "That was during the trial. All the witnesses have now been examined." A Special CBI Court in Bengaluru had on April 17, 2026 sentenced Kulkarni and 15 others to life imprisonment after finding them guilty of conspiring to murder BJP leader Yogesh Gowda, who was hacked to death at a gym in Dharwad on June 15, 2016. The trial court had convicted the accused under Sections 302 (murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the Indian Penal Code after concluding that they had entered into a conspiracy to eliminate Gowda. Besides life imprisonment for murder and conspiracy, the convicts were also sentenced for destruction of evidence, unlawful assembly and rioting. Suspended police officer Channakeshava B Tingarikar (A19) was sentenced to 7 years' imprisonment under Section 201 IPC for destruction of evidence. The trial court directed that all sentences would run concurrently and ordered payment of ₹16 lakh from the fine amount as compensation to Gowda's children. Kulkarni and co-accused Chandrasekhar Indi were acquitted of the charges under the Arms Act. Kulkarni was arrested by the CBI on November 5, 2020, and was granted conditional bail by the Supreme Court in August 2021. However, in June 2025, the Supreme Court cancelled his bail after finding prima facie material suggesting attempts to influence witnesses during the course of the trial. items.title: Delhi High Court orders takedown of derogatory content against cricketer Yuvraj Singh
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday directed the takedown of online content flagged as violating the personality rights of former Indian cricketer Yuvraj Singh. Justice Jyoti Singh has passed an interim injunction order restraining certain social media users from exploiting the cricketer's personality traits. "There can be no doubt that violators of personality and privacy rights need to be dealt with a heavy hand," the Court stated in the order. The Court has directed Amazon Seller Services Private Limited, Flipkart Internet Private Limited and other e-commerce websites to take down the listings of unauthorised merchandise, observing that the listings diminish Singh's commercial value. Further, the Court directed Meta Platforms to take down derogatory online content within 36 hours from receipt of this order. Justice Jyoti Singh On July 29, Justice Singh had said that she is ordering the takedown of such derogatory content. However, the Court clarified that it would not issue a blanket direction covering future content at this stage. The Court said that appropriate directions for the takedown of future content can be issued as and when they are flagged. "For now I am directing the takedown of URLs that are part of the suit. If there is anything that comes up, file your application and I extend injunction after seeing they are infringing," said the Court. The Court added that it will direct the individuals who uploaded content flagged as derogatory to Singh to remove the URLs identified in his suit in a time-bound manner. The Court suggested that if the content is not deleted by its uploaders within the given timeline, Singh can notify the social media platforms and other intermediaries for the removal of such content. The intermediaries have been granted three weeks to file their responses. The matter is next listed on November 13. The Court passed the order on a suit filed by Singh seeking the protection of his personality rights, and the removal of online content found violating these rights. "The contents of the impugned AI-generated posts and deep fake videos are tarnishing the immense goodwill and reputation of the Plaintiff, garnered over the years with hard work and stellar performances in the field of cricket as well as his contribution to social welfare and lowering his image and standing in the eyes of the public," the Court stated.
